title: ‘This is a mistake’: Srikkanth slams India’s ‘fear-driven’ squad for Afghan series
content: Former cricketer Kris Srikkanth criticised India's squad selection for the Afghanistan series. He believes selectors missed an opportunity to test younger players. Srikkanth described the decision as a mistake influenced by recent defeats. The selectors opted for an experienced team instead of experimenting with new talent. This approach was seen as a safe move after losses in Ireland and England.

title: Jeff Bezos' ex-wife sets new record with donations to historically Black colleges
content: MacKenzie Scott has now donated over one billion dollars to historically Black colleges. Her recent forty-two million dollar gift to Elizabeth City State University marked this milestone. Scott has provided significant funding to numerous institutions since 2020. These unrestricted donations empower universities to allocate funds as needed. Her extensive philanthropic efforts support various educational and community initiatives.

title: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith’s message to international students: Study, then return home
content: Alberta's Premier Danielle Smith has made it clear that international students need to leave Canada once their study visas expire. She highlighted that these visas serve as temporary permits meant for academic pursuits, urging students to return to their home countries. This statement follows rising concerns over immigration programs misleading students about potential residency outcomes. With Canada tightening its immigration policies, unauthorized work could lead to serious repercussions.

title: Gold miners breach Indonesian orangutan sanctuary, damaging 14 hectares
content: The Jantho forest reservation in Indonesia, vital for orangutan rehabilitation, is under siege from illegal gold miners. This encroachment places the habitat of critically endangered Sumatran orangutans, rescued from illegal trade, at severe risk. Mining activities have already destroyed approximately fourteen hectares, while toxic runoff threatens the surrounding Krueng Aceh River, endangering both community health and wildlife.

title: Michigan farmer protects 131 acres from housing after buying family land back
content: Michigan farmer John Boyer bought back his family’s 131 acres after the land changed hands over decades. In 2026, he sold its development rights to the Little Traverse Conservancy through a conservation easement, ensuring the property cannot be divided for housing or commercial development. Boyer hopes the farmland remains protected for generations.

title: Sam Altman denies one ChatGPT query uses 6hr shower water, gives almond example
content: Sam Altman refutes claims that AI computing consumes excessive water, emphasizing that contemporary data centers utilize advanced cooling technologies that differ significantly from outdated models. He likens the water consumption of AI systems to that of almond farming, dubbing prevalent narratives as misconceptions. Moreover, he notes that large data centers require a similar amount of water as typical office buildings.

title: Travis Kelce’s $1.5m nonprofit under scrutiny: Why did charity spending raise questions?
content: Travis Kelce’s Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation is facing scrutiny over its reported spending between 2021 and 2024. The nonprofit raised $1.5 million and spent about $1.1 million, with $469,000 listed for management and $446,000 for charity. Kelce’s business manager Aaron Eanes disputed the figures, saying some charitable operational costs were misclassified. He said management fees dropped to zero in 2025 as the foundation works to improve transparency and governance.

title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ $900m partnership: What’s behind the deal?
content: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes are preparing to appear together in a new project tied to their long-standing partnership with a major Kansas City brand valued at around $900 million. Behind-the-scenes footage has already offered a glimpse of the couple during production. The latest appearance adds another chapter to Mahomes’ expanding commercial presence, as the Chiefs quarterback continues to attract major brands despite ongoing debate surrounding his recent NFL performances.

title: Naomi Osaka vs Serena Williams: How did their 2018 US Open final change her career?
content: Naomi Osaka made history in 2018 by winning her first Grand Slam title against Serena Williams. This pivotal match showcased her exceptional composure, turning what could have been a tumultuous finale into a career-defining moment. Her triumph set the stage for her ascent as a preeminent figure in tennis and a celebrated athlete from Japan, earning her admiration worldwide and paving the way for more significant victories.

title: ‘Someone is smoking weed’: Sabalenka stops US Open match mid-game — Watch
content: In an unexpected turn during her US Open match, world number one Aryna Sabalenka was distracted by a strong cannabis odor. Noticing the smell while facing Kamilla Rakhimova, she promptly alerted the chair umpire, leading to a consultation with tournament officials. This peculiar incident is reportedly linked to park regulations in the area. Despite the unusual challenge, Sabalenka maintained her composure and triumphed in straight sets to advance.

title: Happy Teachers' Day 2026: 100+ wishes, messages, quotes and WhatsApp status
content: On Saturday, September 5, 2026, we will celebrate Teachers Day in honor of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, the second president of India. This special day brings forth an extensive selection of more than 110 wishes, quotes, and messages designed to resonate with different sentiments across various platforms. The article offers a rich compilation to help you express your appreciation in a heartfelt manner.

title: Why IIT and IIM students are ditching backpacks for buckets and bicycles
content: The “No-Bag Day” trend is gaining popularity on Indian higher-education campuses, with students at IIT Bombay and IIM Lucknow replacing conventional backpacks with buckets, umbrellas, cardboard boxes, chairs and even bicycles. The student-led activity offers a playful break from demanding academic routines while encouraging creativity and camaraderie. Inspired by the international “Anything But a Bag Day” concept, the trend has also appeared at other Indian colleges, turning an ordinary campus day into a memorable experience.

title: Rahul vs Vijay: Can TVK chief do what Kejriwal could not?
content: Tamil Nadu's chief minister Vijay faces a political challenge regarding national leadership.  His party, TVK, and the Congress coalition are debating the 2029 prime ministerial candidate.  Vijay's rise disrupts traditional state politics and sparks national aspirations.  He must balance state leadership with a broader political project.  This dynamic creates tension within the ruling coalition. Is he ready to have a direct contest with Rahul Gandhi?

title: Breather for India? Trump's Russia sanctions bill may be put off till Nov; here's why

title: Jaishankar says India in touch with Russia, Ukraine to help end war
content: India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar is actively engaging with both Ukraine and Russia. He is exploring potential ideas and suggestions to help end the ongoing conflict. India believes dialogue and diplomacy are essential for resolving the protracted war. Minister Jaishankar met with Ukrainian leadership and Polish officials during his visit. Discussions also covered trade, technology, and security cooperation between India and Poland.

title: ‘Developed countries must take lead': India calls for climate finance after Nepal flood
content: India urged developed nations to lead emissions cuts and aid developing countries.  Developed nations must provide finance and technology transfer for climate action.  India expressed solidarity and support for Nepal's reconstruction efforts after floods.  Nepal clarified no compensation was sought from India or other major economies.  Both nations agreed to collaborate on Himalayan climate change impacts.

title: SAI creates ‘Little Japan’: Indian athletes get taste of Asian Games life in containers
content: The Sports Authority of India has launched a unique facility inspired by Japanese culture, featuring accommodations fashioned from shipping containers. These two-bedroom units are equipped with contemporary amenities, immersing athletes in Japanese cuisine such as ramen, sushi, and tempura crafted by skilled chefs. This endeavour is geared towards helping athletes adjust to Japan ahead of the upcoming Asian Games, while also providing permanent transit housing for visiting families.

title: Nearly $750bn shield: How India built record forex reserves amid US-Iran war
content: How has the RBI managed to secure high forex reserves in times of global economic uncertainty? What’s worked for India and why does the rise in forex cover matter? And, importantly, is it sustainable?

content: China's surge in artificial intelligence innovations is driving a remarkable expansion of its computing infrastructure. Ulanqab, located in Inner Mongolia, is positioning itself as a pivotal hub for AI computing, capitalizing on its vast renewable energy resources and favorable climate for data centers. This enhanced computing capability is fulfilling the increasing AI requirements of the nation.

Currently, Sindarov is concentrating on these events but acknowledges Gukesh's prowess and is committed to delivering his best play. Their historic duel, featuring two talented twenty-year-olds, is slated for November in Geneva.

title: Bargaining tactics? Why BJP's 'solo pitch' in Punjab may have message for Akalis

Conversely, Shiromani Akali Dal officials are pushing to renew their partnership with the BJP. Currently, the BJP appears to have the upper hand in negotiations, although both factions remain open to the possibility of joining forces down the line.

title: ‘Focus on cricket, not the noise,’ Mithali tells India ahead of Pakistan clash
content: India secured a Women's Asia Cup semifinal spot after a dominant win.  The team now prepares for a crucial match against Pakistan in Dubai.  Former captain Mithali Raj advises players to focus on cricket and their roles.  She believes India is the favourite to win the upcoming match.  The Asia Cup serves as a vital platform for developing teams and reclaiming the title.

title: 'I chanted Hare Krishna for 9 days': Nepal worker rescued from tunnel on Janmashtami

He communicated with a few nearby workers while trapped in darkness. Two workers were rescued alive, and search operations continue for others. Hesson is now focused on fine-tuning the squad for the final Test, emphasizing a well-rounded bowling lineup with greater diversity, while integrating new talent to enhance team balance.

title: Ladakh residents to get ownership rights over 60,000 acres of barren land
content: ladakh residents will now have rights over barren lands or wastelands owned by govt . the rules provide a framework for granting proprietary rights on up to 10 acres of eligible Nautor land holdings to the occupants across all seven districts of the Union Territory .

title: Coal stock at thermal plants plummets, 'critical' at 50 units
content: 50 plants classified as having 'critically low' inventories as on sept 2 . the plants, with a combined capacity of around 224 GW, had 28.2 million tonnes of coal as of Wednesday, 48% of the prescribed requirement of 58.7 MT .

title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial ends in mistrial as jury fails to reach verdict
content: the mistrial leaves the case unresolved and allows prosecutors to retry the 36-year-old former labor and delivery nurse . the deliberations took a dramatic turn late in the week when the judge said he would declare a misrial on Friday . but then changed course and gave Clancy's defense attorney an opportunity to appeal to the top court .

title: SC awards pension to Mumbai engineer who forged ST certificate
content: Shirish P Patil got a certificate in 1984 by identifying himself as belonging to the 'Tokre Koli' Scheduled Tribe community . he misplaced the original ST certificate but managed to secure a fresh one from the sub-divisional magistrate in Oct 2000 .
